text.p: These are the leading stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- S E R B I A -
POLITIKA

- Situation in Yugoslavia's economy is more favourable now than in previous months but shortage of working capital and high public expenditure limit its revival, says the Institute for Market Research (IZIT).
- Yugoslav Supreme Defence Council meets, discusses financial situation in the army and promotes a number of superior officers.

- It is evident that former Yugoslav republics wish to resolve the problem of succession of ex-Yugoslavia partially and to give it a political dimension, says the Yugoslav government group for succession.
- Yugoslavia and Greece initial agreement on avoidance of double taxation.
- Construction and development of gas pipeline network is one of the major objectives of Yugoslavia's energy policy, says Yugoslav Energy Minister Rade Filipovic.
- Yugoslav businessmen call for gradual liberalisation of trade to protect exhausted Yugoslav economy.
- Shipbuilding company Begej from Zrenjanin has completed a third vessel worth over 10 million German marks for Norwegian Boreal shipping-Berger.
- Polish shareholding company Rafako plans to conclude $3.5 million worth of deals this year for supplying parts for Yugoslavia's thermoelectric power plants.
- Health workers' trade unions say they will end strike next Monday if all workers receive the first part of their April wages by that time.
- Yugoslav information minister Goran Matic says it is necessary to set up Yugoslav Radio Television (JRT).
NASA BORBA

- American company Milicon international cellular, SA (MIC) offers to purchase stake in Serbia's postal company PTT Srbije at better conditions than the Italian firm STET, says BK Group in its letter sent to the Serbian government.
- Yugoslav government to make major changes in foreign trade system and adopt anti-dumping measures at the end of July, says Yugoslav foreign trade minister Borislav Vukovic.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Yugoslav airlines JAT plane sequestered at Athens airport because it carried Macedonia airlines insignia. The plane had been rented by the Macedonian airlines earlier.
BORBA
- Serbian government central coordinating team says expansion of exports is the main task of economic policy in the coming period.
DNEVNI TELEGRAF
- Socialist Party of Serbia from Kosovo says Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic will visit the region while the president's office denies it.
- Television station BK TV reported that it had dismissed 100 employees and planned to dismiss another 173.
- M O N T E N E G R O -
POBJEDA

- Montenegrin police minister Filip Vujanovic reacted to allegations from the president's office that he was not a man of his word. Vujanovic said these were "hasty allegations motivated by politcal hatred". He said he would again propose Vukasin Maras as head of Security police, while Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic asks for Maras's replacement.
- Podgorica branch of Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) proposed Momir Bulatovic as presidential candidate in the republican elections.
- University of Montenegro will enrol 1,950 students this year.
